# `nlink-lab wait`

Block until a lab is deployed (`wait -L LAB`), or until conditions hold in one of its nodes: a TCP listener, a command, a file, a listening port, a spawned process's log line or stable fd count, all within one `--timeout`. Exit 124 on timeout.

```bash
nlink-lab wait -L wan -t 60s                       # its deploy finished
sudo nlink-lab wait server --tcp 8080 --exec 'curl -sf localhost:8080/health'
sudo nlink-lab wait server --pid 4242 --log 'listening on' -t 10s
```

## Reference

<!-- cli-ref:start (generated by `nlink-lab docs-gen`; do not edit) -->

```text
Wait for a lab to be deployed, or for conditions in a node.

`wait -L LAB` waits until LAB is deployed. `wait NODE --tcp 8080 --exec 'curl -sf localhost/health'` waits until every condition holds in NODE, all within one `--timeout`; `--log`, `--fd-stable` (and optionally `--listening`) look at a spawned `--pid`.

Usage: nlink-lab wait [OPTIONS] [NODE]

Arguments:
  [NODE]
          The node the conditions are checked in. Without it, wait for the lab to be deployed (name it: -L, NLINK_LAB or `use`)

Options:
  -L, --lab <LAB>
          The lab. Default: `$NLINK_LAB`, then the one `nlink-lab use` selected, then the only running lab

      --tcp <[IP:]PORT>
          A TCP listener: `PORT` (on 127.0.0.1), `IP:PORT`, `[IPv6]:PORT`

      --exec <CMD>
          A command that exits 0 (run with `sh -c`)

      --file <PATH>
          A file that exists

      --listening <PORT>
          A TCP listener on PORT, of any process of the node (of `--pid`'s when it is given). Reads the socket table, connects to nothing

      --log <REGEX>
          A line of the `--pid` process's stdout or stderr that matches

      --fd-stable <DURATION>
          The `--pid` process's open-fd count, unchanged this long (a heuristic: prefer `--log` or `--listening`)

      --pid <PID>
          The spawned process `--log`, `--fd-stable` and `--listening` look at (a PID `spawn` printed)

  -t, --timeout <DURATION>
          How long to wait for all of them
          
          [default: 30s]

  -i, --interval <DURATION>
          How often to look
          
          [default: 500ms]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

<!-- cli-ref:end -->
